text.title: API Contract Pattern Selection Core Rules
text.summary: Seven rules constraining the contract-style verdict. Each one rules a style in or out on a property of that style's wire format or tooling, not on taste: type-only contracts need a shared build, gRPC needs a browser proxy, GraphQL needs cost control, codegen needs a schema document.

rule.statement: If any expected consumer is written in a language other than the server's, the verdict MUST be a style with a language-neutral schema document: openapi-3.1, graphql-sdl, or grpc. trpc and undocumented json-rpc are invalid verdicts in that case, regardless of consumer_count.

rationale.source: tRPC documentation — 'TypeScript on both ends, no code generation'

rule.rationale: tRPC publishes no wire schema; its contract is the exported `AppRouter` TypeScript type. A Python or Swift consumer has literally nothing to compile against, so the "contract" reduces to hand-copied JSON shapes.

rule.statement: A trpc verdict is valid only when client and server compile in the same TypeScript build (monorepo with project references or a workspace package) AND deploy together. If the client can be released against a server version it was not compiled against, pick openapi-3.1 instead.

rationale.source: tRPC documentation — type inference across the client/server boundary

rule.rationale: The type check happens at the client's build time against the server source it had then. Independently deployed clients therefore get zero compile-time signal for a renamed field; the break surfaces at runtime as a failed Zod parse or an undefined property, in production.

rule.statement: A grpc verdict whose consumer list includes a browser MUST name the translation layer (Envoy grpc-web filter, or Connect/grpc-gateway) and who operates it, as an explicit setup ticket in the artefact.
rule.rationale: Browser fetch/XHR cannot read HTTP/2 trailers, and gRPC carries its status code in the trailer. Without a proxy that folds the trailer into the body, every call fails at the transport layer — this is not tunable from the client side.

rule.statement: A graphql-sdl verdict MUST name three controls in the same artefact: a maximum query depth, a complexity/cost limit with its budget, and either persisted queries or an allow-list for external callers. A GraphQL verdict without all three is rejected.

rationale.source: OWASP API Security Top 10 2023 — API4 Unrestricted Resource Consumption

rule.rationale: One endpoint accepting arbitrary nesting lets a single legitimate-looking query fan out into an exponential resolver tree; per-endpoint rate limiting cannot see it because it is one request. Depth and cost limits are the only place the fan-out is bounded.

rule.statement: If tooling_needs contains sdk-gen, mock-server, contract-test, or doc-portal, the verdict MUST resolve to an artefact a generator can read: an OpenAPI 3.1 document, a GraphQL SDL file, or a .proto file, and the artefact MUST name the file path where it lives in the repo.

rationale.source: OpenAPI Specification 3.1.0 — Schema Object aligned with JSON Schema 2020-12

rule.rationale: Generators consume the document, not the server code. Choose 3.1 rather than 3.0 when the same schemas are reused for runtime validation: 3.0 used a modified JSON Schema subset (its own `nullable`, no `examples` keyword), so a 3.0 document and a JSON Schema validator disagree on the same payload.

rule.statement: When evolution_rate is high (more than one breaking change expected per quarter) and team_boundary is external, the artefact MUST name the change mechanism that goes with the chosen style — URL major version plus a stated deprecation window for openapi-3.1/json-rpc; `@deprecated` on fields plus additive-only evolution for graphql-sdl; reserved field numbers for grpc.

rationale.source: GraphQL Best Practices (graphql.org) — versioning; Protocol Buffers language guide — reserved fields

rule.rationale: Each style has exactly one supported evolution story and they are mutually exclusive. Versioning a GraphQL endpoint pays the schema-flexibility cost and then discards the benefit; reusing a retired protobuf field number silently misinterprets old bytes on the wire as the new type.

rule.statement: Skip when the contract style is not actually open: the API has served production traffic under an existing style for more than six months, or the boundary never leaves the process (an in-repo function call). Emit a structured skip naming which condition held.
rule.rationale: A contract decision on a boundary with live consumers is a migration project, not a selection: the cost is the client rewrite, which this methodology does not estimate. Producing a verdict anyway hands the operator a recommendation whose true price is invisible.
